W22.reasons: Does the 6 Oct rule apply? RG qualifies in substance: its feed is held, and on my own parse and link its statistics equal Sackmann's 2019-2021 rows on all eight counts in 2,732 of 2,740 player rows (the 8 others are RGX). But the rule is stretched when applied to Sackmann's own history. The 6 Oct decision applied it to 2026 rows, after Sackmann's data ends; under 'Not decided' it left 'Sackmann's Roland Garros men's qualifying of 2022-2025 ... flagged and left unchanged until a study measures its effect', and that study (item 6) runs under the 8 Oct three-reviewer rule. The decided bar for changing history rows is the 8 Oct one; extending the source rule to them is the owner's call, not a reading of the 6 Oct text. So I apply the 8 Oct bar. It still confirms most matches, because RG's point record settles most counts physically: (a) serve points: in all 1,488 proposed matches whose MatchBeats holds RG's serve points, the capture passes the integrity test, so RG's serve points are the points played; in the proposed matches of 2022-2025 the row differs in 294 player rows, and holds MORE than RG in 167 of them, in 127 matches (a defect of Sackmann's 2022-2025 rows beyond partial boxes: mostly +1, which no missing point or deuce pair can produce in a coherent capture); (b) break points: my recount from MatchBeats equals RG's statistics in 100% of complete rows (3,738 of 2022-2025) and, where the row differs, always reads RG's value; (c) service games: MatchBeats' count equals the exact count from RG's set scores in 100% of completed rows; the row's differs from it where the proposal changes it. The split's '+' sides are the fault (round 1; Court Vision 2022 215 of 215 decided first-serve readings for RG). Where I narrow: on '-'/'0' sides RG's own record is the one sometimes wrong. The honest tally (referees.py; the lead's E2 drops the 13 matches where a referee reads the row): Court Vision 2022 reads RG's first serves in on 22 of 23 '-' rows and the row's on 1 (van de Zandschulp 2022 R128: the whole split), against 215 of 215 decided '+' rows; the hand charts' contrary readings (2 of 26 on '-', 9 of 121 on '+') are within chart noise (on rows where the row equals RG, a chart is off by one on first serves in 10.6% of the time). With a demonstrated RG error on exactly this kind of side and a mechanism (a mis-keyed serve number in RG's capture, not the row's dominant fault), a '-'/'0' change without a per-row referee is not beyond reasonable doubt. Aces and double faults higher in the row run against the row's systematic undercount and no referee holds one. Matches without a complete capture cannot have their counts settled, nor can a retirement where the row holds more points (RG's capture of 2023 QM088 has no point of the second set; 2024 SM038's ends at 40-15 in the game in progress). The blank row is not corrupt; filling it is the source rule. Nothing is lost by narrowing: of the 234 excluded matches, 100 keep a split row step 2 already confirmed, and they hold few other settled errors (13 serve-point and 27 ace/double-fault-lower rows). Retirements: Sackmann counts only completed games as service games in all 68 retired rows of 2022-2025; MatchBeats' count includes the game in progress at the retirement (+1) in 13 of them, and the proposal takes it, replacing Sackmann's correct count in 8 rows (7 in my scope). My values follow Sackmann's convention. The convention otherwise holds: Sackmann's 2022-2025 service games equal the exact tiebreaks-not-counted count in 3,601 of 3,658 completed rows and never the tiebreaks-counted one. The fallback (the row's own count where MatchBeats misses points) is right in value: in the 12 matches with a file it equals the exact count from RG's score and MatchBeats' first server in all 24 rows; in the 8 without a file the sums equal the non-tie-break games. It is still a mix of sources inside a match, against the 6 Oct 'never mixed inside a match'; all 20 such matches fall outside my scope by T1. Conventions: no default in 2022-2026 (RG's end causes: 46 retirements, all Stage 0 retirements; 12 walkovers); penalty points (MatchBeats code P) are counted as serve points by RG's statistics, as in 2019-2021 when they equalled Sackmann's rows; the awarded points (code F, 2026 QM069) sit in a statistics_short match. SVX.reasons: Corrupt beyond doubt, by four lines of evidence, one of them independent of MatchBeats. (1) The first server is proven twice in every proposed match, with my own parse, links and code. The file's first point opens set 1 and its games alternate in order (the lead's test). Separately, every non-tiebreak game the file holds, placed by the score, implies the same first server. Independent records never contradict it: hand charts agree in 457 of 457 matches they hold (25 of 25 swaps; every chart opens at 0-0 and passes the parity test). Court Vision agrees in 735 of 735 (50 of 50 swaps). (2) Where the file holds the whole match, its own game-by-game count of who served is the truth in 318 of 318 swaps (the rest are retirements). (3) A test from the row's own score and break points alone: each player's non-tiebreak games won equal his service games, minus his service games lost, plus the opponent's. Exchanging the two counts flips the difference, so the test can pass for only one of them. It holds for the truth and fails for Sackmann's row in 323 of 324 swapped matches, including all 323 proposed. On the equal class it holds in 3325 of 3332. In 2 swaps, RG 2019 R32 and R16 (Halep d. Tsurenko 6-2 6-1, Halep d. Swiatek 6-1 6-0), Sackmann's counts even fail B8 today: the loser was broken more times than her recorded service games. The exchange repairs them. (4) Not another error dressed as an exchange: serve points, aces, double faults and serve points won fit the row's box by name strictly better than exchanged in 324 of 324 swaps, so the box itself is not exchanged and the server labels are right. The same test flags exactly the four RGX boxes as exchanged, which validates it. Other attacks: the row's winner equals the Slam's in every swap. The row's score equals the Slam's in 321 of 324 (the 3 others are AO retirements where the file also holds the unfinished game). Files that start late are unproven and not proposed. Files that stop early are 6 retirements, and the truth counts completed games, as Sackmann does. Sackmann's count cannot be the right one: the point record, the hand charts and Court Vision name the first server the file names, not the one Sackmann's counts imply, and the score-and-break identity rejects Sackmann's counts. Tennis My Life's rows equal Sackmann's swapped counts in 182 of 252 and the truth in 68. TML shares the derivation, so it is no independent support for Sackmann. 270 of 324 rows are exactly the count as if the winner had served first. The fix is clear, unique and correct. exchange_svgms exchanges only the two counts. After it, every row reads the truth, totals and B5 are unchanged, and B8 passes in all (2 rows newly). No proposed row takes another correction in the candidate (corrections allow one box correction per row) or an override. The dry run with the build's own apply_row_corrections exchanged 323 rows, all reading the truth after, with 0 other counts changed.
